description: Sliding window aggregator prematurely evicts samples at the exact duration cutoff due to <= operator instead of <.
spec_notes: Window boundaries must retain samples matching exactly timestamp == (now - duration).

tests.test_window_invariant.py:
import pytest
from metric_types import MetricPoint
from monitor import ServiceMonitor


def test_basic_window_aggregation():
    mon = ServiceMonitor(window_sec=10.0)
    avg1 = mon.record(100.0, 50.0)
    assert avg1 == 50.0
    avg2 = mon.record(105.0, 70.0)
    assert avg2 == 60.0


def test_boundary_exact_timestamp_retention():
    mon = ServiceMonitor(window_sec=10.0)
    # Point at t=10.0
    mon.record(10.0, 100.0)
    # Point at t=20.0: cutoff is 20.0 - 10.0 = 10.0.
    # A sample at t=10.0 is inside the 10.0s window [10.0, 20.0] and MUST NOT be evicted!
    avg = mon.record(20.0, 200.0)
    assert len(mon.aggregator.samples) == 2
    assert avg == pytest.approx(150.0)


def test_stale_sample_evicted_past_boundary():
    mon = ServiceMonitor(window_sec=10.0)
    mon.record(10.0, 100.0)
    mon.record(20.1, 200.0)  # t=10.0 is strictly < 20.1 - 10.0 (10.1) -> evicted
    assert len(mon.aggregator.samples) == 1
    assert mon.aggregator.get_average() == 200.0


def test_empty_window_average():
    mon = ServiceMonitor(window_sec=5.0)
    assert mon.aggregator.get_average() == 0.0


def test_multiple_points_same_timestamp():
    mon = ServiceMonitor(window_sec=5.0)
    mon.record(10.0, 20.0)
    mon.record(10.0, 40.0)
    assert mon.aggregator.get_average() == 30.0
